title: feat(fullstack): add virtual:fullstack/no-split-css module for simplified CSS collection
pr_body:
Closes #1243

This PR introduces a new experimental `virtual:fullstack/no-split-css` module that provides a simplified API for collecting all CSS in the server module graph. This addresses use cases where code-splitting by route is not important and a simpler approach is desired.

## What's New

The new `virtual:fullstack/no-split-css` module can be imported from server environments to automatically collect all CSS files. This feature must be explicitly enabled via the `experimental.noSplitCss` flag:

```js
// vite.config.ts
import fullstack from "@hiogawa/vite-plugin-fullstack";

export default {
  plugins: [
    fullstack({
      experimental: {
        noSplitCss: true, // Enable the feature
      },
    }),
  ],
};
```

```js
// entry.server.tsx
import noSplitCss from "virtual:fullstack/no-split-css";

export function renderHtml() {
  return `
    <html>
      <head>
        ${noSplitCss.map(css => 
          `<link rel="stylesheet" href="${css.href}" />`)
        .join('\n')}
      </head>
      <body>...</body>
    </html>
  `;
}
```

## Key Features

- **Experimental**: Must be enabled via `experimental.noSplitCss` option (default: false)
- **Works in both dev and build modes**: Simplifies server CSS integration for both development and production
- **Server-side**: Returns empty array in client environment
- **Comprehensive**: Collects all CSS files from the entire server module graph
- **HMR-compatible**: In dev mode, includes `data-vite-dev-id` attributes for proper hot module replacement
- **Build-optimized**: In build mode, collects CSS from the bundle and generates a manifest
- **Type-safe**: Full TypeScript support with proper type declarations

## Comparison with Existing API

This complements the existing `?assets` query import approach:

| Feature | `?assets` Query | `virtual:fullstack/no-split-css` |
|---------|-----------------|----------------------------------|
| Code-splitting per route | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
| Simplicity | Medium | ✅ High |
| Dev + Build | ✅ Both | ✅ Both |
| Granular control | ✅ High | ❌ Low |
| Requires flag | ❌ No | ✅ Yes (experimental) |

Use `virtual:fullstack/no-split-css` when:
- You don't need per-route code-splitting
- You want the simplest possible setup
- You want unified CSS collection across all routes

Use `?assets` query when:
- You need granular control over asset loading
- Code-splitting by route is important
- You need per-route CSS optimization

## Implementation Details

**Dev mode:**
- Recursively traverses the server module graph
- Collects all CSS imports using Vite's `isCSSRequest()` 
- Skips special CSS queries (`?url`, `?inline`, `?raw`)
- Avoids circular dependencies by skipping virtual asset modules
- Returns normalized URLs with `data-vite-dev-id` for HMR

**Build mode:**
- Tracks environments that use the virtual module
- Collects all CSS from all chunks in the environment bundle
- Adds CSS list to the assets manifest under `__no_split_css__` key
- Generated code imports from the manifest

The module only activates when `experimental.noSplitCss` is enabled.

## Testing

Manually tested to confirm:
- ✅ CSS files are correctly collected from the module graph in dev mode
- ✅ HMR attributes are properly included in dev mode
- ✅ Build mode generates proper manifest structure
- ✅ TypeScript compilation passes
- ✅ No linting errors
- ✅ Works correctly in SSR context
- ✅ Properly guarded behind experimental flag

# vite-plugins

Random collection of vite plugins

## plugins

### [`@hiogawa/vite-rsc`](./packages/rsc)

> [!important]
> `@hiogawa/vite-rsc` is now maintained as Vite's official package [`@vitejs/plugin-rsc`](https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/blob/main/packages/plugin-rsc).

Framework-less Vite RSC plugin

### [`@hiogawa/react-server`](./packages/react-server)

Next.js-like RSC framework on Vite

### [`@hiogawa/vite-plugin-ssr-middleware`](./packages/vite-plugin-ssr-middleware)

Minimal version of [`@vavite/connet`](https://github.com/cyco130/vavite/tree/main/packages/connect)
and [`@vavite/expose-vite-dev-server`](https://github.com/cyco130/vavite/tree/main/packages/expose-vite-dev-server)

## Development

### How to release a package

Example: `packages/rsc`

1. Manually bump `packages/rsc/package.json` version
2. Update changelog via `pnpm changelog packages/rsc`
3. Create a PR and merge to main
4. Locally run `pnpm release packages/rsc`
